chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Maskin, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the sun passes its zenith, the times for Dhuhr and Asr enter. And when the sun sets, the times for Maghrib and the latter 'Isha enter." And as for that which indicates the other time, which is the time for one who prays the voluntary prayers.

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The passing of the sun from its zenith (midday)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific astronomical signs that determine the start times for Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and 'Isha prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational astronomical markers for prayer times, specifically defining Dhuhr and Asr as commencing simultaneously at solar zenith (Zawal) and Maghrib and 'Isha at sunset, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the precise onset of time windows. It further clarifies the distinction between the obligatory prayer periods and the specific window for voluntary (nafl) prayers, a nuance critical for understanding the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding prayer timing.
